# cheat

`cheat` allows you to create and view interactive cheatsheets on the
command-line. It was designed to help remind *nix system administrators of
options for commands that they use frequently, but not frequently enough to
remember.

## Example
The next time you're forced to disarm a nuclear weapon without consulting
Google, you may run:

```sh
cheat tar
```

You will be presented with a cheatsheet resembling the following:

```sh
# To extract an uncompressed archive:
tar -xvf '/path/to/foo.tar'

# To extract a .gz archive:
tar -xzvf '/path/to/foo.tgz'

# To create a .gz archive:
tar -czvf '/path/to/foo.tgz' '/path/to/foo/'

# To extract a .bz2 archive:
tar -xjvf '/path/to/foo.tgz'

# To create a .bz2 archive:
tar -cjvf '/path/to/foo.tgz' '/path/to/foo/'
```

## Installing
See [INSTALLING.md][] for installation and configuration instructions.

## Usage
To view a cheatsheet:

```sh
cheat tar      # a "top-level" cheatsheet
cheat foo/bar  # a "nested" cheatsheet
```

To edit a cheatsheet:

```sh
cheat -e tar     # opens the "tar" cheatsheet for editing, or creates it if it does not exist
cheat -e foo/bar # nested cheatsheets are accessed like this
```

To view the configured cheatpaths:

```sh
cheat -d
```

To list all available cheatsheets:

```sh
cheat -l
```

To briefly list all cheatsheets (names and tags only):

```sh
cheat -b
```

To list all cheatsheets that are tagged with "networking":

```sh
cheat -l -t networking
```

To list all cheatsheets on the "personal" path:

```sh
cheat -l -p personal
```

To search for the phrase "ssh" among cheatsheets:

```sh
cheat -s ssh
```

To search (by regex) for cheatsheets that contain an IP address:

```sh
cheat -r -s '(?:[0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}'
```

Flags may be combined in intuitive ways. Example: to search sheets on the
"personal" cheatpath that are tagged with "networking" and match a regex:

```sh
cheat -p personal -t networking --regex -s '(?:[0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}'
```

## Cheatsheets
Cheatsheets are plain-text files with no file extension, and are named
according to the command used to view them:

```sh
cheat tar     # file is named "tar"
cheat foo/bar # file is named "bar", in a "foo" subdirectory
```

Cheatsheet text may optionally be preceded by a YAML frontmatter header that
assigns tags and specifies syntax:

```
---
syntax: javascript
tags: [ array, map ]
---
// To map over an array:
const squares = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(x => x * x);
```

## Cheatpaths
Cheatsheets are stored on "cheatpaths", which are directories that contain
cheatsheets. Cheatpaths are specified in the `conf.yml` file.

It can be useful to configure `cheat` against multiple cheatpaths. A common
pattern is to store cheatsheets from multiple repositories on individual
cheatpaths:

```yaml
# conf.yml:
# ...
cheatpaths:
  - name: community                   # a name for the cheatpath
    path: ~/documents/cheat/community # the path's location on the filesystem
    tags: [ community ]               # these tags will be applied to all sheets on the path
    readonly: true                    # if true, `cheat` will not create new cheatsheets here

  - name: personal
    path: ~/documents/cheat/personal  # this is a separate directory and repository than above
    tags: [ personal ]
    readonly: false                   # new sheets may be written here
# ...
```

The `readonly` option instructs `cheat` not to edit (or create) any cheatsheets
on the path. This is useful to prevent merge-conflicts from arising on upstream
cheatsheet repositories.

If a user attempts to edit a cheatsheet on a read-only cheatpath, `cheat` will
transparently copy that sheet to a writeable directory before opening it for
editing.

### Directory-scoped Cheatpaths
At times, it can be useful to closely associate cheatsheets with a directory on
your filesystem. `cheat` facilitates this by searching for a `.cheat` directory
in the current working directory and its ancestors (similar to how `git` locates
`.git` directories). The nearest `.cheat` directory found will (temporarily) be
added to the cheatpaths. This means you can place a `.cheat` directory at your
project root and it will be available from any subdirectory within that project.

## Autocompletion
`cheat` can generate shell completion scripts for `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, and
`powershell` via the `--completion` flag:

```sh
cheat --completion bash
cheat --completion zsh
cheat --completion fish
cheat --completion powershell
```

Pipe the output to the appropriate location for your shell. For example:

```sh
# bash (user-local)
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions
cheat --completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/cheat

# bash (system-wide)
cheat --completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/cheat

# zsh (ensure the directory is on your fpath)
cheat --completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_cheat"

# fish
cheat --completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/cheat.fish
```

Completions are dynamically generated and include cheatshee

## Cheatpaths
Cheatsheets are stored on "cheatpaths", which are directories that contain
cheatsheets. Cheatpaths are specified in the `conf.yml` file.

It can be useful to configure `cheat` against multiple cheatpaths. A common
pattern is to store cheatsheets from multiple repositories on individual
cheatpaths:

```yaml
# conf.yml:
# ...
cheatpaths:
  - name: community                   # a name for the cheatpath
    path: ~/documents/cheat/community # the path's location on the filesystem
    tags: [ community ]               # these tags will be applied to all sheets on the path
    readonly: true                    # if true, `cheat` will not create new cheatsheets here

  - name: personal
    path: ~/documents/cheat/personal  # this is a separate directory and repository than above
    tags: [ personal ]
    readonly: false                   # new sheets may be written here
# ...
```

The `readonly` option instructs `cheat` not to edit (or create) any cheatsheets
on the path. This is useful to prevent merge-conflicts from arising on upstream
cheatsheet repositories.

If a user attempts to edit a cheatsheet on a read-only cheatpath, `cheat` will
transparently copy that sheet to a writeable directory before opening it for
editing.

At times, it can be useful to closely associate cheatsheets with a directory on
your filesystem. `cheat` facilitates this by searching for a `.cheat` directory
in the current working directory and its ancestors (similar to how `git` locates
`.git` directories). The nearest `.cheat` directory found will (temporarily) be
added to the cheatpaths. This means you can place a `.cheat` directory at your
project root and it will be available from any subdirectory within that project.

        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))
        if not in_cheatpaths:
            if stripped.startswith("cheatpaths:"):
                in_cheatpaths = True
                i += 1; continue
            if ":" in stripped:
                k, v = stripped.split(":", 1)
                k = k.strip(); v = v.strip()
                if k == "editor": cfg.editor = unquote(v)
                elif k == "pager": cfg.pager = unquote(v)
                elif k == "colorize": cfg.colorize = parse_bool(v)
                elif k == "style": cfg.style = unquote(v)
                elif k == "formatter": cfg.formatter = unquote(v)
            i += 1; continue
        # inside cheatpaths. Only top-level-ish list items and their fields matter.
        if indent == 0 and not stripped.startswith("-") and ":" in stripped:
            in_cheatpaths = False
            continue
        if stripped.startswith("-"):
            if cur is not None:
                cfg.cheatpaths.append(cur)
            cur = {"name":"", "path":".", "tags":[], "readonly":False}
            rest = stripped[1:].strip()
            if rest and ":" in rest:
                k, v = rest.split(":", 1)
                k = k.strip(); v = v.strip()
                if k == "name": cur["name"] = unquote(v)
                elif k == "path": cur["path"] = unquote(v) or "."
                elif k == "tags": cur["tags"] = parse_list_value(v)
                elif k == "readonly": cur["readonly"] = parse_bool(v)
            i += 1; continue
        if cur is not None and ":" in stripped:
            k, v = stripped.split(":", 1)
            k = k.strip(); v = v.strip()
            if k == "name": cur["name"] = unquote(v)
            elif k == "path": cur["path"] = unquote(v) or "."
            elif k == "readonly": cur["readonly"] = parse_bool(v)
            elif k == "tags":
                if v:
                    cur["tags"] = parse_list_value(v)
                else:
                    arr=[]; j=i+1
                    while j < len(lines):
                        s2 = lines[j].strip()
                        if not s2 or s2.startswith("#"):
                            j += 1; continue
                        if s2.startswith("-"):
                            arr.append(unquote(s2[1:].strip()))
                            j += 1; continue
                        break
                    cur["tags"] = arr
                    i = j; continue
        i += 1
    if cur is not None:
        cfg.cheatpaths.append(cur)

    # Validate editor after environment overrides like the original does.
    if not (os.environ.get("VISUAL") or os.environ.get("EDITOR") or cfg.editor):
        raise CheatError("failed to load config: no editor set")

    cps=[]
    for d in cfg.cheatpaths:
        name = d.get("name", "")
        if not name:
            raise CheatError("failed to load config: config error: cheatpath name cannot be empty")
        p = d.get("path") or "."
        expanded = os.path.expanduser(p)
        display = expanded
        # Environment variables are not expanded by the real config examples, but
        # expanding user paths is convenient and matches common usage.
        if not os.path.isdir(expanded):
            eprint(f"WARNING: cheatpath '{p}' does not exist, skipping")
            continue
        cps.append(CheatPath(name=name, path=p, tags=list(d.get("tags", [])), readonly=bool(d.get("readonly", False)), scan_path=expanded, display_path=display))
    cfg.cheatpaths = cps
    add_cwd_cheatpath(cfg)
    if not cfg.cheatpaths:
        raise CheatError("failed to load config: config error: no cheatpaths specified")
    return cfg


def add_cwd_cheatpath(cfg):
    cur = os.getcwd()
    while True:
        cand = os.path.join(cur, ".cheat")
        if os.path.isdir(cand):
            # Avoid adding it twice if explicitly configured.
            if not any(os.path.abspath(cp.scan_path) == os.path.abspath(cand) for cp in cfg.cheatpaths):
                cfg.cheatpaths.append(CheatPath(name="cwd", path=cand, tags=[], readonly=False, scan_path=cand, display_path=cand))
            return
        parent = os.path.dirname(cur)
        if parent == cur:
            return
        cur = parent

def parse_frontmatter(title, file_display, data):
    syntax=""; tags=[]; body=data
    if data.startswith("---\n") or data.startswith("---\r\n"):
        lines = data.splitlines(True)
        end_idx = None
        pos = len(lines[0])
        for idx in range(1, len(lines)):
            if lines[idx].strip() == "---":
                end_idx = idx
                break
            pos += len(lines[idx])
        if end_idx is None:
            raise ParseError("failed to parse front-matter: failed to delimit frontmatter")
        header = "".join(lines[1:end_idx])
        body = "".join(lines[end_idx+1:])
        hlines = header.splitlines()
        i=0
        while i < len(hlines):
            s=hlines[i].strip()
            if not s or s.startswith("#"):
                i+=1; continue
            if ":" in s:
                k,v=s.split(":",1); k=k.strip(); v=v.strip()
                if k == "syntax": syntax = unquote(v)
                elif k == "tags":
                    if v:
                        try:
                            tags = parse_list_value(v)
                        except Exception:
                            # Match the common yaml error for scalar tags closely enough.
                            val = unquote(v)
                            raise ParseError("failed to parse front-matter: failed to unmarshal frontmatter: yaml: unmarshal errors:\n  line 1: cannot unmarshal !!str `" + val + "` into []string")
                    else:
                        arr=[]; j=i+1
                        while j < len(hlines):
                            s2=hlines[j].strip()
                            if s2.startswith("-"):
                                arr.append(unquote(s2[1:].strip())); j+=1; continue
                            if not s2:
                                j+=1; continue
                            break
                        tags=arr; i=j; continue
            i+=1
    return body, syntax, tags


def load_sheets(cfg):
    sheets=[]
    for idx, cp in enumerate(cfg.cheatpaths):
        root = cp.scan_path
        for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
            dirnames[:] = sorted([d for d in dirnames if d != ".git"])
            for fn in sorted(filenames):
                # Sheets have no extension; hidden leaf files are ignored.
                if fn.startswith(".") or "." in fn:
                    continue
                real = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
                if not os.path.isfile(real):
                    continue
                rel = os.path.relpath(real, root)
                title = rel.replace(os.sep, "/")
                display_file = os.path.join(cp.display_path, rel).replace(os.sep, "/")
                try:
                    data = open(real, "r", encoding="utf-8").read()
                except UnicodeDecodeError:
                    data = open(real, "r", errors="replace").read()
                try:
                    content, syntax, ftags = parse_frontmatter(title, display_file, data)
                except ParseError as ex:
                    raise CheatError(f"failed to list cheatsheets: failed to load cheatsheets: failed to load sheet: {title}, path: {display_file}, err: {ex}")
                tags = sorted(set(cp.tags + ftags))
                sheets.append(Sheet(title=title, file=display_file, real_file=real, path_name=cp.name, path_index=idx, tags=tags, content=content, syntax=syntax, readonly=cp.readonly))
    sheets.sort(key=lambda s: (s.title, s.path_index, s.file))
    return sheets


def validate_path_filter(cfg, opts):
    p = opts.get("path")
    if p and not any(cp.name == p for cp in cfg.cheatpaths):
        raise CheatError(f"invalid option --path: cheatpath does not exist: {p}")


def apply_filters(sheets, opts, title_filter=None, for_tags=False):
    res = list(sheets)
    if opts.get("path"):
        res = [s for s in res if s.path_name == opts["path"]]
    if opts.get("tag") and not for_tags:
        res = [s for s in res if opts["tag"] in s.tags]
    if title_filter:
        low = title_filter.lower()
        res = [s for s in res if low in s.title.lower()]
    return res


def table_list(sheets, brief=False):
    if brief:
        rows = [(s.title, ",".join(s.tags)) for s in sheets]
        col1 = max([len("title:")] + [len(r[0]) for r in rows]) + 1
        out = f"{'title:':<{col1}}tags:\n"
        for t,tags in rows:
            out += f"{t:<{col1}}{tags}\n"
        return out
    rows = [(s.title, s.file, ",".join(s.tags)) for s in sheets]
    col1 = max([len("title:")] + [len(r[0]) for r in rows]) + 1
    col2 = max([len("file:")] + [len(r[1]) for r in rows]) + 1
    out = f"{'title:':<{col1}}{'file:':<{col2}}tags:\n"
    for t,f,tags in rows:
        out += f"{t:<{col1}}{f:<{col2}}{tags}\n"
    return out


def dirs_output(cfg):
    names = [cp.name for cp in cfg.cheatpaths]
    width = max(len(n) for n in names) + 2
    out=""
    for cp in cfg.cheatpaths:
        out += f"{(cp.name + ':'):<{width}}{cp.display_path}\n"
    return out


def maybe_color_heading(title, path, color):
    if color:
        return f"{title} \x1b[2m({path})\x1b[0m"
    return f"{title} ({path})"


def indent_content(content):
    # Prefix each logical line with a tab. splitlines(True) preserves final newlines.
    if content == "":
        return "\t"
    parts = content.splitlines(True)
    return "".join("\t" + p for p in parts)


def multi_sheet_output(sheets, color=False):
    chunks=[]
    for s in sheets:
        chunks.append(maybe_color_heading(s.title, s.path_name, color) + "\n" + indent_content(colorize_content(s.content, s.syntax) if color else s.content))
    return "\n\n".join(chunks)


def colorize_content(content, syntax=""):
    # A lightweight approximation of the default terminal256 formatter: comments grey,
    # other non-empty lines white. This preserves plain text when color is disabled.
    out=[]
    for line in content.splitlines(True):
        core = line[:-1] if line.endswith("\n") else line
        nl = "\n" if line.endswith("\n") else ""
        if core.startswith("#"):
            out.append(f"\x1b[38;5;242m{core}\x1b[0m\x1b[38;5;231m\x1b[0m{nl}")
        elif core:
            out.append(f"\x1b[38;5;231m{core}\x1b[0m{nl}")
        else:
            out.append(nl)
    return "".join(out)


def output_with_pager(cfg, text):
    pager = cfg.pager or ""
    if not pager or pager == "cat":
        sys.stdout.write(text)
        return 0
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(pager, input=text, text=True, shell=True)
        return p.returncode
    except Exception:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
        return 0


def list_tags(sheets):
    tags = sorted({t for s in sheets for t in s.tags})
    return "".join(t + "\n" for t in tags)


def find_matching_for_view(sheets, title, opts):
    exact = [s for s in sheets if s.title == title]
    exact = apply_filters(exact, opts)
    return exact


def view_sheet(cfg, sheets, title, opts):
    matches = find_matching_for_view(sheets, title, opts)
    color = opts.get("colorize") or cfg.colorize
    if opts.get("all"):
        return multi_sheet_output(matches, color), 0
    if not matches:
        return f"No cheatsheet found for '{title}'.\n", 2
    # most local path wins: highest path index. If equal, stable last.
    s = sorted(matches, key=lambda x: (x.path_index, x.file))[-1]
    return (colorize_content(s.content, s.syntax) if color else s.content), 0


def search_sheets(cfg, sheets, opts):
    phrase = opts.get("search", "")
    filtered = apply_filters(sheets, opts)
    if opts.get("regex"):
        try:
            rgx = re.compile(phrase)
        except re.error as ex:
            raise CheatError(f"failed to compile regexp: {phrase}, error parsing regexp: {ex}: `{phrase}`")
        matches = [s for s in filtered if rgx.search(s.content)]
    else:
        low=phrase.lower()
        matches=[s for s in filtered if low in s.content.lower()]
    return multi_sheet_output(matches, opts.get("colorize") or cfg.colorize), 0


def validate_sheet_name(name):
    if os.path.isabs(name):
        raise CheatError("invalid cheatsheet name: cheatsheet name cannot be an absolute path")
    if ".." in name:
        raise CheatError("invalid cheatsheet name: cheatsheet name cannot contain '..'")
    for part in name.split("/"):
        if part.startswith("."):
            raise CheatError("invalid cheatsheet name: cheatsheet name cannot start with '.' (hidden files are not supported)")


def editor_cmd(cfg):
    return os.environ.get("VISUAL") or os.environ.get("EDITOR") or cfg.editor


def edit_sheet(cfg, sheets, name, opts):
    validate_sheet_name(name)
    matches = find_matching_for_view(sheets, name, opts)
    target = None
    if matches:
        s = sorted(matches, key=lambda x: (x.path_index, x.file))[-1]
        if not s.readonly:
            target = s.real_file
        else:
            # copy to most local writable path among the selected paths
            writable = [cp for cp in cfg.cheatpaths if not cp.readonly and (not opts.get("path") or cp.name == opts.get("path"))]
            if not writable:
                raise CheatError("failed to get writeable path: no writeable cheatpaths found")
            cp = writable[-1]
            target = os.path.join(cp.scan_path, *name.split("/"))
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copyfile(s.real_file, target)
    else:
        writable = [cp for cp in cfg.cheatpaths if not cp.readonly and (not opts.get("path") or cp.name == opts.get("path"))]
        if not writable:
            raise CheatError("failed to get writeable path: no writeable cheatpaths found")
        cp = writable[-1]
        target = os.path.join(cp.scan_path, *name.split("/"))
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)
    cmd = editor_cmd(cfg)
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(f"{cmd} {shell_quote(target)}", shell=True)
    except Exception as ex:
        raise CheatError(f"failed to edit cheatsheet: {ex}")
    if r.returncode != 0:
        raise CheatError(f"failed to edit cheatsheet: exit status {r.returncode}")
    return "", 0


def shell_quote(s):
    return "'" + s.replace("'", "'\\''") + "'"


def remove_sheet(sheets, name, opts):
    validate_sheet_name(name)
    matches = find_matching_for_view(sheets, name, opts)
    if not matches:
        raise CheatError(f"No cheatsheet found for '{name}'.", 2)
    s = sorted(matches, key=lambda x: (x.path_index, x.file))[-1]
    if s.readonly:
        raise CheatError(f"cheatsheet '{name}' is read-only.")
    try:
        os.remove(s.real_file)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise CheatError(f"No cheatsheet found for '{name}'.", 2)
    return "", 0


def update_paths(cfg, opts):
    cps = [cp for cp in cfg.cheatpaths if not opts.get("path") or cp.name == opts["path"]]
    out=[]
    for cp in cps:
        # Use git itself to decide whether this is a work tree.
        chk = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", cp.scan_path, "rev-parse", "--is-inside-work-tree"], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        if chk.returncode != 0:
            out.append(f"{cp.name}: skipped (not a git repository)\n")
            continue
        out.append(f"{cp.name}: ")
        pull = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", cp.scan_path, "pull", "--ff-only"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
        txt = pull.stdout.strip()
        out.append(txt + ("\n" if txt else "\n"))
    return "".join(out), 0


def completion_script(shell):
    if shell not in ("bash", "zsh", "fish", "powershell"):
        raise CheatError(f"unsupported shell: {shell} (valid: bash, zsh, fish, powershell)")
    # Compact but functional enough completion scripts, with the same identifying header.
    if shell == "bash":
        return """# bash completion V2 for cheat                                -*- shell-script -*-

_cheat_completion()
{
    local cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    COMPREPLY=( $( COMP_WORDS="${COMP_WORDS[*]}" cheat __completeNoDesc "$cur" 2>/dev/null | sed '/^:/d' ) )
}
complete -F _cheat_completion cheat
"""
    if shell == "zsh":
        return """#compdef cheat
compdef _cheat cheat

# zsh completion for cheat                                -*- shell-script -*-

_cheat() {
  local -a vals
  vals=(${(f)"$(cheat __completeNoDesc "${words[-1]}" 2>/dev/null | sed '/^:/d')"})
  compadd -- $vals
}
"""
    if shell == "fish":
        return """# fish completion for cheat                                -*- shell-script -*-

complete -c cheat -f -a '(cheat __completeNoDesc (commandline -ct) 2>/dev/null | string match -v ":*")'
"""
    return """# powershell completion for cheat                                -*- shell-script -*-

Register-ArgumentCompleter -CommandName cheat -ScriptBlock {
    param($wordToComplete, $commandAst, $cursorPosition)
    cheat __completeNoDesc $wordToComplete 2>$null | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^:' }
}
"""


def completion_endpoint(args, no_desc=False):
    if len(args) < 1:
        raise CheatError("requires at least 1 arg(s), only received 0")
    # Complete values for current flag.
    prev = None
    cur = args[-1]
    if len(args) >= 2:
        prev = args[-2]
    try:
        cfg = parse_config_file(find_config_path()) if find_config_path() else None
        sheets = load_sheets(cfg) if cfg else []
    except Exception:
        cfg=None; sheets=[]
    vals=[]
    directive=4
    if prev in ("-p", "--path") or (args and args[0] in ("-p", "--path")):
        vals = [cp.name for cp in (cfg.cheatpaths if cfg else [])]
    elif prev in ("-t", "--tag") or (args and args[0] in ("-t", "--tag")):
        vals = sorted({t for s in sheets for t in s.tags})
    elif prev == "--completion" or (args and args[0] == "--completion"):
        vals=[]; directive=0
    else:
        vals = [s.title for s in sheets]
    return "".join(v + "\n" for v in vals) + f":{directive}\n", 0, directive


def parse_args(argv):
    opts = {"all":False,"brief":False,"colorize":False,"conf":False,"directories":False,
            "help":False,"init":False,"list":False,"regex":False,"tags":False,"update":False,
            "version":False,"completion":None,"edit":None,"path":None,"rm":None,"search":None,"tag":None}
    positionals=[]
    long_bool={"all":"all","brief":"brief","colorize":"colorize","conf":"conf","directories":"directories","help":"help","init":"init","list":"list","regex":"regex","tags":"tags","update":"update","version":"version"}
    long_str={"completion":"completion","edit":"edit","path":"path","rm":"rm","search":"search","tag":"tag"}
    short_bool={"a":"all","b":"brief","c":"colorize","d":"directories","h":"help","l":"list","r":"regex","T":"tags","u":"update","v":"version"}
    short_str={"e":"edit","p":"path","s":"search","t":"tag"}
    i=0
    while i < len(argv):
        a=argv[i]
        if a == "--":
            positionals += argv[i+1:]; break
        if a.startswith("--") and len(a)>2:
            body=a[2:]
            val=None
            if "=" in body:
                body,val=body.split("=",1)
            if body in long_bool:
                opts[long_bool[body]]=True
                i+=1; continue
            if body in long_str:
                if val is None:
                    if i+1 >= len(argv):
                        raise CheatError(f"flag needs an argument: --{body}")
                    val=argv[i+1]; i+=1
                opts[long_str[body]]=val
                i+=1; continue
            raise CheatError(f"unknown flag: --{body}")
        if a.startswith("-") and a != "-":
            body=a[1:]
            j=0
            while j < len(body):
                ch=body[j]
                if ch in short_bool:
                    opts[short_bool[ch]]=True; j+=1; continue
                if ch in short_str:
                    if j+1 < len(body):
                        val=body[j+1:]; j=len(body)
                    else:
                        if i+1 >= len(argv):
                            raise CheatError(f"flag needs an argument: '{ch}' in -{ch}")
                        val=argv[i+1]; i+=1; j=len(body)
                    opts[short_str[ch]]=val; continue
                raise CheatError(f"unknown shorthand flag: '{ch}' in -{ch}")
            i+=1; continue
        positionals.append(a); i+=1
    return opts, positionals


def main(argv):
    # Hidden completion subcommands are parsed by Cobra before normal flags.
    if argv and argv[0] in ("__complete", "__completeNoDesc"):
        try:
            out, rc, directive = completion_endpoint(argv[1:], argv[0] == "__completeNoDesc")
            sys.stdout.write(out)
            names={0:"ShellCompDirectiveDefault",4:"ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp"}
            sys.stderr.write(f"Completion ended with directive: {names.get(directive, directive)}\n")
            return rc
        except CheatError as ex:
            if str(ex): eprint(str(ex))
            return ex.code
    try:
        opts, pos = parse_args(argv)
        # Argument count is validated for normal commands, but version/help/init ignore extras.
        if opts["version"]:
            sys.stdout.write(VERSION + "\n"); return 0
        if opts["help"]:
            sys.stdout.write(HELP); return 0
        if opts["init"]:
            sys.stdout.write(init_text()); return 0
        if opts.get("completion") is not None:
            sys.stdout.write(completion_script(opts["completion"])); return 0
        if len(pos) > 1 and not (opts.get("search") is not None or opts.get("edit") is not None or opts.get("rm") is not None):
            raise CheatError(f"accepts at most 1 arg(s), received {len(pos)}")

        cfg = load_config_or_install()
        validate_path_filter(cfg, opts)
        if opts["conf"]:
            sys.stdout.write(cfg.path + "\n"); return 0
        sheets = load_sheets(cfg)

        if opts["directories"]:
            sys.stdout.write(dirs_output(cfg)); return 0
        if opts["edit"] is not None:
            out, rc = edit_sheet(cfg, sheets, opts["edit"], opts); sys.stdout.write(out); return rc
        if opts["brief"]:
            filtered = apply_filters(sheets, opts, pos[0] if pos else None)
            if not filtered: return 2
            sys.stdout.write(table_list(filtered, True)); return 0
        if opts["list"]:
            filtered = apply_filters(sheets, opts, pos[0] if pos else None)
            if not filtered: return 2
            sys.stdout.write(table_list(filtered, False)); return 0
        if opts["tags"]:
            filtered = apply_filters(sheets, opts, None, for_tags=True)
            sys.stdout.write(list_tags(filtered)); return 0
        if opts["rm"] is not None:
            out, rc = remove_sheet(sheets, opts["rm"], opts); sys.stdout.write(out); return rc
        if opts["update"]:
            out, rc = update_paths(cfg, opts); sys.stdout.write(out); return rc
        if opts["search"] is not None:
            out, rc = search_sheets(cfg, sheets, opts); return output_with_pager(cfg, out) or rc
        if pos:
            out, rc = view_sheet(cfg, sheets, pos[0], opts)
            if rc == 0:
                return output_with_pager(cfg, out) or 0
            else:
                sys.stdout.write(out); return rc
        sys.stdout.write(HELP); return 0
    except CheatError as ex:
        if str(ex):
            # Some not-found messages are printed to stdout by view, but to stderr by rm.
            eprint(str(ex))
        return ex.code

def strip_inline_comment(s):
    out=[]; sq=dq=False; esc=False
    for ch in s:
        if esc:
            out.append(ch); esc=False; continue
        if ch == "\\" and dq:
            out.append(ch); esc=True; continue
        if ch == "'" and not dq:
            sq = not sq; out.append(ch); continue
        if ch == '"' and not sq:
            dq = not dq; out.append(ch); continue
        if ch == "#" and not sq and not dq:
            break
        out.append(ch)
    return "".join(out).rstrip()


def unquote(s):
    s = strip_inline_comment(s.strip())
    if len(s) >= 2 and ((s[0] == s[-1] == '"') or (s[0] == s[-1] == "'")):
        return s[1:-1]
    return s


def parse_bool(v):

def parse_list_value(v):
    v = strip_inline_comment(v.strip())
    if v == "" or v == "[]":
        return []
    if v.startswith("[") and v.endswith("]"):
        inner = v[1:-1].strip()
        if not inner:
            return []
        return [unquote(x.strip()) for x in inner.split(",") if unquote(x.strip()) != ""]
    raise ValueError(v)

def parse_frontmatter(title, file_display, data):
    syntax=""; tags=[]; body=data
    if data.startswith("---\n") or data.startswith("---\r\n"):
        lines = data.splitlines(True)
        end_idx = None
        pos = len(lines[0])
        for idx in range(1, len(lines)):
            if lines[idx].strip() == "---":
                end_idx = idx
                break
            pos += len(lines[idx])
        if end_idx is None:
            raise ParseError("failed to parse front-matter: failed to delimit frontmatter")
        header = "".join(lines[1:end_idx])
        body = "".join(lines[end_idx+1:])
        hlines = header.splitlines()
        i=0
        while i < len(hlines):
            s=hlines[i].strip()
            if not s or s.startswith("#"):
                i+=1; continue
            if ":" in s:
                k,v=s.split(":",1); k=k.strip(); v=v.strip()
                if k == "syntax": syntax = unquote(v)
                elif k == "tags":
                    if v:
                        try:
                            tags = parse_list_value(v)
                        except Exception:
                            # Match the common yaml error for scalar tags closely enough.
                            val = unquote(v)
                            raise ParseError("failed to parse front-matter: failed to unmarshal frontmatter: yaml: unmarshal errors:\n  line 1: cannot unmarshal !!str `" + val + "` into []string")
                    else:
                        arr=[]; j=i+1
                        while j < len(hlines):
                            s2=hlines[j].strip()
                            if s2.startswith("-"):
                                arr.append(unquote(s2[1:].strip())); j+=1; continue
                            if not s2:
                                j+=1; continue
                            break
                        tags=arr; i=j; continue
            i+=1
    return body, syntax, tags


def load_sheets(cfg):
    sheets=[]
    for idx, cp in enumerate(cfg.cheatpaths):
        root = cp.scan_path
        for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
            dirnames[:] = sorted([d for d in dirnames if d != ".git"])
            for fn in sorted(filenames):
                # Sheets have no extension; hidden leaf files are ignored.
                if fn.startswith(".") or "." in fn:
                    continue
                real = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
                if not os.path.isfile(real):
                    continue
                rel = os.path.relpath(real, root)
                title = rel.replace(os.sep, "/")
                display_file = os.path.join(cp.display_path, rel).replace(os.sep, "/")
                try:
                    data = open(real, "r", encoding="utf-8").read()
                except UnicodeDecodeError:
                    data = open(real, "r", errors="replace").read()
                try:
                    content, syntax, ftags = parse_frontmatter(title, display_file, data)
                except ParseError as ex:
                    raise CheatError(f"failed to list cheatsheets: failed to load cheatsheets: failed to load sheet: {title}, path: {display_file}, err: {ex}")
                tags = sorted(set(cp.tags + ftags))
                sheets.append(Sheet(title=title, file=display_file, real_file=real, path_name=cp.name, path_index=idx, tags=tags, content=content, syntax=syntax, readonly=cp.readonly))
    sheets.sort(key=lambda s: (s.title, s.path_index, s.file))
    return sheets


def validate_path_filter(cfg, opts):
    p = opts.get("path")
    if p and not any(cp.name == p for cp in cfg.cheatpaths):
        raise CheatError(f"invalid option --path: cheatpath does not exist: {p}")


def apply_filters(sheets, opts, title_filter=None, for_tags=False):
    res = list(sheets)
    if opts.get("path"):
        res = [s for s in res if s.path_name == opts["path"]]
    if opts.get("tag") and not for_tags:
        res = [s for s in res if opts["tag"] in s.tags]
    if title_filter:
        low = title_filter.lower()
        res = [s for s in res if low in s.title.lower()]
    return res


def table_list(sheets, brief=False):
    if brief:
        rows = [(s.title, ",".join(s.tags)) for s in sheets]
        col1 = max([len("title:")] + [len(r[0]) for r in rows]) + 1
        out = f"{'title:':<{col1}}tags:\n"
        for t,tags in rows:
            out += f"{t:<{col1}}{tags}\n"
        return out
    rows = [(s.title, s.file, ",".join(s.tags)) for s in sheets]
    col1 = max([len("title:")] + [len(r[0]) for r in rows]) + 1
    col2 = max([len("file:")] + [len(r[1]) for r in rows]) + 1
    out = f"{'title:':<{col1}}{'file:':<{col2}}tags:\n"
    for t,f,tags in rows:
        out += f"{t:<{col1}}{f:<{col2}}{tags}\n"
    return out


def dirs_output(cfg):
    names = [cp.name for cp in cfg.cheatpaths]
    width = max(len(n) for n in names) + 2
    out=""
    for cp in cfg.cheatpaths:
        out += f"{(cp.name + ':'):<{width}}{cp.display_path}\n"
    return out


def maybe_color_heading(title, path, color):
    if color:
        return f"{title} \x1b[2m({path})\x1b[0m"
    return f"{title} ({path})"


def indent_content(content):
    # Prefix each logical line with a tab. splitlines(True) preserves final newlines.
    if content == "":
        return "\t"
    parts = content.splitlines(True)
    return "".join("\t" + p for p in parts)


def multi_sheet_output(sheets, color=False):
    chunks=[]
    for s in sheets:
        chunks.append(maybe_color_heading(s.title, s.path_name, color) + "\n" + indent_content(colorize_content(s.content, s.syntax) if color else s.content))
    return "\n\n".join(chunks)


def colorize_content(content, syntax=""):
    # A lightweight approximation of the default terminal256 formatter: comments grey,
    # other non-empty lines white. This preserves plain text when color is disabled.
    out=[]
    for line in content.splitlines(True):
        core = line[:-1] if line.endswith("\n") else line
        nl = "\n" if line.endswith("\n") else ""
        if core.startswith("#"):
            out.append(f"\x1b[38;5;242m{core}\x1b[0m\x1b[38;5;231m\x1b[0m{nl}")
        elif core:
            out.append(f"\x1b[38;5;231m{core}\x1b[0m{nl}")
        else:
            out.append(nl)
    return "".join(out)


def output_with_pager(cfg, text):
    pager = cfg.pager or ""
    if not pager or pager == "cat":
        sys.stdout.write(text)
        return 0
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(pager, input=text, text=True, shell=True)
        return p.returncode
    except Exception:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
        return 0


def list_tags(sheets):
    tags = sorted({t for s in sheets for t in s.tags})
    return "".join(t + "\n" for t in tags)


def find_matching_for_view(sheets, title, opts):
    exact = [s for s in sheets if s.title == title]
    exact = apply_filters(exact, opts)
    return exact


def view_sheet(cfg, sheets, title, opts):
    matches = find_matching_for_view(sheets, title, opts)
    color = opts.get("colorize") or cfg.colorize
    if opts.get("all"):
        return multi_sheet_output(matches, color), 0
    if not matches:
        return f"No cheatsheet found for '{title}'.\n", 2
    # most local path wins: highest path index. If equal, stable last.
    s = sorted(matches, key=lambda x: (x.path_index, x.file))[-1]
    return (colorize_content(s.content, s.syntax) if color else s.content), 0


def search_sheets(cfg, sheets, opts):
    phrase = opts.get("search", "")
    filtered = apply_filters(sheets, opts)
    if opts.get("regex"):
        try:
            rgx = re.compile(phrase)
        except re.error as ex:
            raise CheatError(f"failed to compile regexp: {phrase}, error parsing regexp: {ex}: `{phrase}`")
        matches = [s for s in filtered if rgx.search(s.content)]
    else:
        low=phrase.lower()
        matches=[s for s in filtered if low in s.content.lower()]
    return multi_sheet_output(matches, opts.get("colorize") or cfg.colorize), 0


def validate_sheet_name(name):

            raise CheatError("invalid cheatsheet name: cheatsheet name cannot start with '.' (hidden files are not supported)")

def edit_sheet(cfg, sheets, name, opts):
    validate_sheet_name(name)
    matches = find_matching_for_view(sheets, name, opts)
    target = None
    if matches:
        s = sorted(matches, key=lambda x: (x.path_index, x.file))[-1]
        if not s.readonly:
            target = s.real_file

            writable = [cp for cp in cfg.cheatpaths if not cp.readonly and (not opts.get("path") or cp.name == opts.get("path"))]
            if not writable:
                raise CheatError("failed to get writeable path: no writeable cheatpaths found")
            cp = writable[-1]
            target = os.path.join(cp.scan_path, *name.split("/"))
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copyfile(s.real_file, target)
    else:
        writable = [cp for cp in cfg.cheatpaths if not cp.readonly and (not opts.get("path") or cp.name == opts.get("path"))]
        if not writable:
            raise CheatError("failed to get writeable path: no writeable cheatpaths found")
        cp = writable[-1]
        target = os.path.join(cp.scan_path, *name.split("/"))
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)

    try:
        r = subprocess.run(f"{cmd} {shell_quote(target)}", shell=True)
    except Exception as ex:
        raise CheatError(f"failed to edit cheatsheet: {ex}")
    if r.returncode != 0:
        raise CheatError(f"failed to edit cheatsheet: exit status {r.returncode}")
    return "", 0


def shell_quote(s):
    return "'" + s.replace("'", "'\\''") + "'"


def remove_sheet(sheets, name, opts):
    validate_sheet_name(name)
    matches = find_matching_for_view(sheets, name, opts)
    if not matches:
        raise CheatError(f"No cheatsheet found for '{name}'.", 2)
    s = sorted(matches, key=lambda x: (x.path_index, x.file))[-1]
    if s.readonly:
        raise CheatError(f"cheatsheet '{name}' is read-only.")
    try:
        os.remove(s.real_file)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise CheatError(f"No cheatsheet found for '{name}'.", 2)
    return "", 0


def update_paths(cfg, opts):
    cps = [cp for cp in cfg.cheatpaths if not opts.get("path") or cp.name == opts["path"]]
    out=[]
    for cp in cps:
        # Use git itself to decide whether this is a work tree.
        chk = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", cp.scan_path, "rev-parse", "--is-inside-work-tree"], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        if chk.returncode != 0:
            out.append(f"{cp.name}: skipped (not a git repository)\n")
            continue
        out.append(f"{cp.name}: ")
        pull = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", cp.scan_path, "pull", "--ff-only"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
        txt = pull.stdout.strip()
        out.append(txt + ("\n" if txt else "\n"))
    return "".join(out), 0


def completion_script(shell):
    if shell not in ("bash", "zsh", "fish", "powershell"):
        raise CheatError(f"unsupported shell: {shell} (valid: bash, zsh, fish, powershell)")
    # Compact but functional enough completion scripts, with the same identifying header.
    if shell == "bash":
        return """# bash completion V2 for cheat                                -*- shell-script -*-

_cheat_completion()
{
    local cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    COMPREPLY=( $( COMP_WORDS="${COMP_WORDS[*]}" cheat __completeNoDesc "$cur" 2>/dev/null | sed '/^:/d' ) )
}
complete -F _cheat_completion cheat
"""
    if shell == "zsh":
        return """#compdef cheat
compdef _cheat cheat

# zsh completion for cheat                                -*- shell-script -*-

_cheat() {
  local -a vals
  vals=(${(f)"$(cheat __completeNoDesc "${words[-1]}" 2>/dev/null | sed '/^:/d')"})
  compadd -- $vals
}
"""
    if shell == "fish":
        return """# fish completion for cheat                                -*- shell-script -*-

complete -c cheat -f -a '(cheat __completeNoDesc (commandline -ct) 2>/dev/null | string match -v ":*")'
"""
    return """# powershell completion for cheat                                -*- shell-script -*-

Register-ArgumentCompleter -CommandName cheat -ScriptBlock {
    param($wordToComplete, $commandAst, $cursorPosition)
    cheat __completeNoDesc $wordToComplete 2>$null | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^:' }
}
"""


def completion_endpoint(args, no_desc=False):
    if len(args) < 1:
        raise CheatError("requires at least 1 arg(s), only received 0")
    # Complete values for current flag.
    prev = None
    cur = args[-1]
    if len(args) >= 2:
        prev = args[-2]
    try:
        cfg = parse_config_file(find_config_path()) if find_config_path() else None
        sheets = load_sheets(cfg) if cfg else []
    except Exception:
        cfg=None; sheets=[]
    vals=[]
    directive=4
    if prev in ("-p", "--path") or (args and args[0] in ("-p", "--path")):
        vals = [cp.name for cp in (cfg.cheatpaths if cfg else [])]
    elif prev in ("-t", "--tag") or (args and args[0] in ("-t", "--tag")):
        vals = sorted({t for s in sheets for t in s.tags})
    elif prev == "--completion" or (args and args[0] == "--completion"):
        vals=[]; directive=0
    else:
        vals = [s.title for s in sheets]
    return "".join(v + "\n" for v in vals) + f":{directive}\n", 0, directive


def parse_args(argv):
    opts = {"all":False,"brief":False,"colorize":False,"conf":False,"directories":False,
            "help":False,"init":False,"list":False,"regex":False,"tags":False,"update":False,
            "version":False,"completion":None,"edit":None,"path":None,"rm":None,"search":None,"tag":None}
    positionals=[]
    long_bool={"all":"all","brief":"brief","colorize":"colorize","conf":"conf","directories":"directories","help":"help","init":"init","list":"list","regex":"regex","tags":"tags","update":"update","version":"version"}
    long_str={"completion":"completion","edit":"edit","path":"path","rm":"rm","search":"search","tag":"tag"}
    short_bool={"a":"all","b":"brief","c":"colorize","d":"directories","h":"help","l":"list","r":"regex","T":"tags","u":"update","v":"version"}
    short_str={"e":"edit","p":"path","s":"search","t":"tag"}
    i=0
    while i < len(argv):
        a=argv[i]
        if a == "--":
            positionals += argv[i+1:]; break
        if a.startswith("--") and len(a)>2:
            body=a[2:]
            val=None
            if "=" in body:
                body,val=body.split("=",1)
            if body in long_bool:
                opts[long_bool[body]]=True
                i+=1; continue
            if body in long_str:
                if val is None:
                    if i+1 >= len(argv):
                        raise CheatError(f"flag needs an argument: --{body}")
                    val=argv[i+1]; i+=1
                opts[long_str[body]]=val
                i+=1; continue
            raise CheatError(f"unknown flag: --{body}")
        if a.startswith("-") and a != "-":
            body=a[1:]
            j=0
            while j < len(body):
                ch=body[j]
                if ch in short_bool:
                    opts[short_bool[ch]]=True; j+=1; continue
                if ch in short_str:
                    if j+1 < len(body):
                        val=body[j+1:]; j=len(body)
                    else:
                        if i+1 >= len(argv):
                            raise CheatError(f"flag needs an argument: '{ch}' in -{ch}")
                        val=argv[i+1]; i+=1; j=len(body)
                    opts[short_str[ch]]=val; continue
                raise CheatError(f"unknown shorthand flag: '{ch}' in -{ch}")
            i+=1; continue
        positionals.append(a); i+=1
    return opts, positionals


def main(argv):
    # Hidden completion subcommands are parsed by Cobra before normal flags.
    if argv and argv[0] in ("__complete", "__completeNoDesc"):
        try:
            out, rc, directive = completion_endpoint(argv[1:], argv[0] == "__completeNoDesc")
            sys.stdout.write(out)
            names={0:"ShellCompDirectiveDefault",4:"ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp"}
            sys.stderr.write(f"Completion ended with directive: {names.get(directive, directive)}\n")
            return rc
        except CheatError as ex:
            if str(ex): eprint(str(ex))
            return ex.code
    try:
        opts, pos = parse_args(argv)
        # Argument count is validated for normal commands, but version/help/init ignore extras.
        if opts["version"]:
            sys.stdout.write(VERSION + "\n"); return 0
        if opts["help"]:
            sys.stdout.write(HELP); return 0
        if opts["init"]:
            sys.stdout.write(init_text()); return 0
        if opts.get("completion") is not None:
            sys.stdout.write(completion_script(opts["completion"])); return 0
        if len(pos) > 1 and not (opts.get("search") is not None or opts.get("edit") is not None or opts.get("rm") is not None):
            raise CheatError(f"accepts at most 1 arg(s), received {len(pos)}")

        cfg = load_config_or_install()
        validate_path_filter(cfg, opts)
        if opts["conf"]:
            sys.stdout.write(cfg.path + "\n"); return 0
        sheets = load_sheets(cfg)

        if opts["directories"]:
            sys.stdout.write(dirs_output(cfg)); return 0
        if opts["edit"] is not None:
            out, rc = edit_sheet(cfg, sheets, opts["edit"], opts); sys.stdout.write(out); return rc
        if opts["brief"]:
            filtered = apply_filters(sheets, opts, pos[0] if pos else None)
            if not filtered: return 2
            sys.stdout.write(table_list(filtered, True)); return 0
        if opts["list"]:
            filtered = apply_filters(sheets, opts, pos[0] if pos else None)
            if not filtered: return 2
            sys.stdout.write(table_list(filtered, False)); return 0
        if opts["tags"]:
            filtered = apply_filters(sheets, opts, None, for_tags=True)
            sys.stdout.write(list_tags(filtered)); return 0
        if opts["rm"] is not None:
            out, rc = remove_sheet(sheets, opts["rm"], opts); sys.stdout.write(out); return rc
        if opts["update"]:
            out, rc = update_paths(cfg, opts); sys.stdout.write(out); return rc
        if opts["search"] is not None:
            out, rc = search_sheets(cfg, sheets, opts); return output_with_pager(cfg, out) or rc
        if pos:
            out, rc = view_sheet(cfg, sheets, pos[0], opts)
            if rc == 0:
                return output_with_pager(cfg, out) or 0
            else:
                sys.stdout.write(out); return rc
        sys.stdout.write(HELP); return 0
    except CheatError as ex:
        if str(ex):
            # Some not-found messages are printed to stdout by view, but to stderr by rm.
            eprint(str(ex))
        return ex.code

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
